# Qwen3-0.6B · B200 · Dynamo vLLM aggregated KVBM

_One-GPU proof of concept for Dynamo's aggregated vLLM KVBM path (upstream
`examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_kvbm.sh`): Qwen3-0.6B, a 20 GB CPU KVBM tier, and the repository's pinned
9,600-token agentic-code trace. Config: [`recipe.yaml`](recipe.yaml) · Numbers: `RESULTS.md`._

## How to reproduce

Three steps, run from `inference/k8s_recipes/`. Nothing else is needed — `install` provisions the cluster side and `run` drives the whole lifecycle.

```bash
# 1 · pick your cluster → writes cluster-profiles/<profile>.env  (one-time, per cluster)
scripts/llmb-k8s init

# 2 · install THIS recipe: namespace + secrets + model-cache PVC + weights  (safe to re-run)
scripts/llmb-k8s install <profile> --recipes qwen3-0-6b-b200-vllm-agg-kvbm-pareto

# 3 · run it: preflight → serve → sweep → results (GPUs freed on the way out)
scripts/llmb-k8s run recipes/llm-perf/kvbm/qwen3-0-6b-b200-vllm-agg-kvbm-pareto <profile> --teardown --fetch
```

Numbers land in [`RESULTS.md`](RESULTS.md) (100% code-generated by `llmb-k8s publish`). Stuck, or need the underlying primitives? [`docs/CLI.md`](../../../../docs/CLI.md) · [`TROUBLESHOOTING.md`](../../../../TROUBLESHOOTING.md)
<!-- REPRODUCE:END -->

## What to read

**TPS/GPU** for capacity, **TTFT/TPOT** against both SLA limits, and **% incomplete/cancelled**. KVBM
counters are enabled (`DYN_KVBM_METRICS=true`) — use them to confirm the CPU tier is actually populated
rather than inferring cache behaviour from latency alone.

## Cell-specific notes

The amd64/B200 hardware sibling of the arm64/GB300 KVBM cell — model, trace, serving args and sweep are held
identical so hardware behaviour can be compared without silently changing the workload. To rank them:
`scripts/llmb-k8s compare recipes/llm-perf/kvbm/qwen3-0-6b-b200-vllm-agg-kvbm-pareto recipes/llm-perf/kvbm/qwen3-0-6b-gb300-vllm-agg-kvbm-pareto`.

Two behaviours are handled automatically by this cell's recipe and need no operator action: the pre-sweep
`/metrics` gate DEGRADES to a warning (a Dynamo front-end re-exports the raw `vllm:*` groups under
`dynamo_frontend_*`/`kvbm_*` names; perf comes from the aiperf client, not `/metrics`), and
`bench.colocate_with_server: true` pins the bench pod to the server's node so the ReadWriteOnce model-cache
PVC cannot Multi-Attach-deadlock.
